sentence: Living in the house alone does not give you that authority.
mustFindings: Item 1 answer 'Living in the house alone does not give you that authority.' states a legal conclusion about authority to sell as certain, with no confirm-with-a-professional language and no ledger claim. 'that authority' also has no antecedent in the answer, so it does not stand alone. Reword to name who to confirm with (a real estate attorney or title company) and say who may sign depends on how title is held, without a closed list of roles.
shouldFindings: The statement that living in a house does not give authority to sell is a general legal principle that no cited ledger claim supports (the brief cites no claim for authority).
